housing: Maidstone is Kent's county town, with Victorian terraces near the centre, large post-war estates to the south-east and many new-build estates on the town's edges. About one in six households rent privately, below the national share. The rural south of the borough has Weald villages with timber-framed houses and oast conversions, many off mains gas.
checkinTips: New-build estates on the town's edges: photograph snagging marks, sealant and any settlement cracks so they are recorded before the tenancy.
Riverside flats near the Medway: note any damp or condensation and record fob, key and parking permit counts.
Victorian terraces in Fant and Tovil: photograph sash or replacement windows, rear yards and any damp in back rooms.
Timber-framed and weatherboarded cottages in the Weald villages: record beams, uneven floors, low doorways and the state of external boards.
Rural homes off mains gas: photograph the oil tank, its gauge level and the boiler service label.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or safety concerns can contact Maidstone Borough Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect privately rented homes.
